content.text:
**What I'd tell my son:** I didn't decide anything. I'll ask you first, and maybe the bank. Harel's money is managed under several kinds of savings plans. The page showed me one kind, "קופת גמל להשקעה", with 16 tracks. Each charges about half a percent a year: "0.54%" to "0.61% מההיסכון" and "0% מההפקדה". The one that sounded closest to my deposit was "כספי (שקלי)". Under "תשואה שנתית ממוצעת" it shows "4.25%" for 3 years and "3.08%" for 5 years. That number decided it for me, but I don't know what my own deposit pays, so I can't say if it's more. And many tracks have no return at all, only "פחות מ־3 שנים".

**What I looked at, in order:**
1. The top: "הראל", and "מנתוני רשות שוק ההון". That sounds official, so I trusted it.
2. The row of products. "קופת גמל להשקעה 16" was already chosen. Next to it were "קרן השתלמות", "קרן חדשה מקיפה" and "חיסכון לכל ילד 4". The last one is for the grandchildren and I'd want to know more.
3. The table. I read the track names from the right. I picked out "אג"ח סחיר" because government bonds are safe, but its return just says "פחות מ־3 שנים". Then "כספי (שקלי)".
4. One big number stayed with me: "24.04%" on "מניות". That's shares, so it's not for me. I skipped the "עוקב מדד S&P 500" lines: English letters, and "עוקב מדד" means nothing to me.
5. On the second screen I read the sentence under the table: "התשואה היא תשואת עבר... היא לא אומרת מה יקרה בהמשך". Good that they say it.
6. I didn't open the folded headings "קרנות מחקות", "קרנות סל", "מרכזות לפיצויים", or the documents list under "מה כתוב במסמכים של הראל".

**What I didn't understand:** "חשיפה למניות ולמט"ח", "מט"ח", the coloured rings, "סחיר", "מחקות", "קרנות סל", "PF-10", "123 ממקור / מחושב / הזנה", and the little arrows next to the fund numbers. Is "0.54% מההיסכון" taken every year? I assume so.

**What I couldn't read well:** The whole page is black with grey writing. The small lines under the table were too small and pale: "התקרה בחוק: 1.05%..." and "בנוסף לדמי הניהול יורדות... הוצאות ישירות". So were the footer and the line under the heading listing the companies. The dark page tired my eyes.

**Where I worried:** The table is full of percentages and coloured circles, and that made me nervous. Nothing tells me whether this is as safe as a deposit, and nothing compares it to the bank. I still don't know whether my bank is taking too much from me.
